transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, my sleep is just all broken up lately. I work overnight shifts as a personal care aide, and when I get off work, I just lie there wide awake. And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, I wake up feeling scared. It's like I never even rested at all.
When you wake up feeling scared, are you waking up from vivid, frightening dreams?
No, it's not really dreams. I don't remember having any nightmares or anything like that. I just... I wake up and the feeling is already there. Just this sudden, heavy fear, but I don't know why.
Do you ever experience these sudden surges of intense fear or panic while you are awake during the day?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel down and just... drained all the time, but I don't get those sudden panic attacks or anything during the day. It's really just that weird, scared feeling when I wake up.
Do you sleep better when you have a stretch of days off or are on vacation?

No, it doesn't really matter if I have days off. Like I said before, my sleep is just completely broken up now. Even if I don't have to work my overnight shift, I still just lie there wide awake. And when I do finally drift off, I still wake up feeling scared and like I haven't rested at all. It's the same whether I'm working or not.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy doing?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I still like the things I usually do. I don't think I've lost interest in them or anything.
Has anyone ever told you that you scream, cry out, or thrash around when you wake up feeling scared?
No, nobody has ever said anything like that to me. I mean... I don't think I do. I just wake up with that awful, scared feeling, but I'm not yelling or throwing myself around as far as I know.
How long have you been having this trouble with your sleep?

Um, it's been about... a year and two months. Yeah, a little over a year. It started right around the time my agency changed my schedule. They put me on rotating overnight shifts, and they gave me all this extra paperwork to do on top of it.
Do you struggle with severe sleepiness or falling asleep while you are working your overnight shifts?
No, I don't really struggle with that. I mean, I'm tired, but I don't fall asleep while I'm working or anything. I just stay awake and do my job.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about not being able to sleep, or about how it will affect your next day?

Not really. I mean... I know I'm probably not going to sleep well, but I don't sit around stressing about it. It just kind of is what it is at this point. I still have to go in and get through my shift either way, so I don't really spend time worrying about how tired I'll be.
How is this broken sleep impacting your day-to-day life, such as your work performance or your personal relationships?

It's affecting things a lot. I mean... I can't really keep up with my care visits safely anymore. My supervisor actually had to step in and stop me during a care-plan visit recently because I just got too overwhelmed and stuck, and I couldn't even finish it. 

And outside of work, I've pretty much pulled away from everything. I stopped going to church, dropped my Zumba classes, and I'm not doing my mentoring anymore. It takes everything I have just to manage work and get back home.
Did you ever have any problems with your sleep before your agency switched you to these rotating overnight shifts?

No, I didn't. I used to sleep just fine. All of this... it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It started right when my agency changed my schedule to those rotating overnight shifts and added on a bunch of extra paperwork. Before that happened, I didn't have any issues with my sleep.
